name: Grand Auxerrois

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards.

notes: Traditional red Burgundy is known for savory fleshiness and farmyard aromas, though modern styles are often lighter, cleaner and more fruit-forward.
In good years red Burgundy ages well, gaining complex fruit and forest floor flavors and often peaking 15 to 20 years after the vintage.
Grand cru wines are made for cellaring and usually need at least five to seven years.
Aligoté makes light whites with slightly herbal flavor and higher acidity than Chardonnay.

blurb.text: A Burgundy area in the Yonne. Its village appellations are Saint-Bris, Vézelay and Irancy, and it also has regional Bourgogne names such as Bourgogne Côtes d'Auxerre and Bourgogne Tonnerre.
